text: The report describes its H2 contribution as extending the prophage–AMR correlation to 4,770 species vs ~100 and controlling genome count rather than capsule presence.
quote: Our work extends this by demonstrating the prophage-AMR correlation at much larger scale (4,770 species vs ~100) and showing it persists after controlling for genome count rather than capsule presence.
heading: Literature Context

text: The report cites Chen et al. (2018) as finding ARG–mobile genetic element co-occurrence on assembled river-metagenome contigs, including prophage associations.
quote: Chen et al. (2018) ([DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envpol.2018.11.024)) found ARG-MGE co-occurrence on assembled contigs from river metagenomes, including associations with prophages.
heading: Literature Context

text: The report interprets its pangenome analysis as confirming that ARG–prophage associations occur in reference genomes rather than only environmental assemblies.
quote: Our pangenome-scale analysis provides a genomic-reference counterpart to their metagenomic observations, confirming that the ARG-prophage association is encoded in reference genomes, not just environmental assemblies.
heading: Literature Context

text: The report cites Bearson & Brunelle (2015) as demonstrating fluoroquinolone-induced prophage in multidrug-resistant Salmonella that enables phage-mediated resistance-plasmid transduction.
quote: Bearson & Brunelle (2015) ([DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijantimicag.2015.04.008)) demonstrated that fluoroquinolone exposure induces prophage in multidrug-resistant *Salmonella*, enabling phage-mediated transduction of resistance plasmids.
heading: Literature Context

text: The report cites Fisarova et al. (2021) as showing high-frequency antimicrobial-resistance plasmid transduction by Staphylococcus epidermidis phages, providing mechanistic evidence for phage-mediated AMR spread.
quote: Fisarova et al. (2021) ([DOI](https://doi.org/10.1128/mSphere.00223-21)) showed that *S. epidermidis* phages transduce antimicrobial resistance plasmids at high frequency, providing additional mechanistic evidence for phage-mediated AMR spread in clinically relevant organisms.
heading: Literature Context

text: The report describes its analysis as the first pangenome-scale analysis of prophage–AMR gene-neighborhood co-localization across 100 species (1,953 genomes, 36,041 AMR gene instances).
quote: **Scale**: This is the first pangenome-scale analysis of prophage-AMR gene-neighborhood co-localization across 100 species (1,953 genomes, 36,041 AMR gene instances).
heading: Novel Contribution

text: Prophage density explains 30% of variance in AMR breadth across 4,770 species, which the report describes as a stronger predictor than previously documented.
quote: **Species-level predictor**: Prophage density explains 30% of variance in AMR breadth across 4,770 species — a stronger predictor than previously documented.
heading: Novel Contribution

text: The reversal of the proximity–accessory association at very close range (≤5 genes) suggests that immediate phage neighbors are core phage genes rather than acquired cargo, a nuance the report says prior contig-level studies missed.
quote: **Threshold sensitivity**: The reversal of the proximity-accessory association at very close range (≤5 genes) suggests that immediate phage neighbors are core phage genes, not acquired cargo. This nuance was not captured in prior contig-level studies.
heading: Novel Contribution

text: The report measures AMR–prophage distances in ordinal gene positions parsed from gene_id rather than base pairs, so true genomic distances may differ.
quote: **Gene position proxy**: Distances are in ordinal gene positions parsed from gene_id format, not base-pair resolution. True genomic distances may differ.
heading: Limitations

text: The report identifies prophages through keyword/Pfam matching on bakta_annotations rather than dedicated tools such as PHASTER or geNomad, potentially including false positives such as phage-defense systems and missing divergent prophages.
quote: **Prophage identification**: Uses keyword/Pfam matching on bakta_annotations rather than dedicated prophage prediction tools (e.g., PHASTER, geNomad). May include false positives (e.g., phage-defense systems) and miss divergent prophages.
heading: Limitations

text: The co-localization analysis sampled 20 genomes per species, and the report says exhaustive analysis of all 293K genomes would strengthen its findings.
quote: **Sampling**: 20 genomes sampled per species for co-localization (NB02). While representative, exhaustive analysis of all 293K genomes would strengthen the findings.
heading: Limitations

text: Core/accessory labels depend on species-level pangenome calling with motupan, so the same gene can have different conservation status in different species.
quote: **Core/accessory labels**: Depend on species-level pangenome calling (motupan). The same gene in different species may have different conservation status.
heading: Limitations

text: The report could not test the fitness-cost hypothesis H3 because of limited overlap between Fitness Browser organisms and GTDB species.
quote: **Fitness data gap**: H3 could not be tested due to limited overlap between fitness browser organisms and GTDB species.
heading: Limitations

text: The species-level H2 association does not prove phage-mediated AMR transfer because species with open pangenomes may independently accumulate prophages and AMR genes.
quote: **Correlation vs causation**: The H2 association does not prove phage-mediated AMR transfer; species with open pangenomes may independently accumulate both prophages and AMR genes.
